newsitem.title: USA: Bank regulators to focus on prevention - Chicago Fed.
newsitem.headline: Bank regulators to focus on prevention - Chicago Fed.

text.p: Banks regulators should focus on preventing crises in a banking industry faced with the challenges of new financial products, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Michael Moskow said on Thursday.

"Interest rate and exchange rate volatility have increased, competition among financial institutions has intensified, and new financial products are being developed continuously," Moskow told a conference on banking co-sponsored by the Chicago Fed and the World Bank, in Lake Bluff, Ill.
The text of his speech was made available in New York.

"Supervisors need to adapt regulations to changing market realities, improve the infrastructure undergirding the financial system, and coordinate supervisory and regulatory efforts internationally," Moskow said. "I hope we will focus on preventing bank crises and work to take advantage of market forces and incentive-compatible approaches whenever possible."
He also elaborated on three proposals to reform the U.S. deposit insurance system.
"The narrow bank proposal would limit insurance coverage to a narrow class of deposits which would be covered by extremely safe and liquid assets," Moskow said.
"The second proposal is to decrease the safety net and increase the role of disclosure and market discipline.
"The third proposal is increasing the role of subordinated debt in the capital structure of banks."
Moskow said the third proposal may prove too intrusive and "may actually prevent capital flows from flowing to valuable investment projects."

The Chicago Fed president said his own experience in the field of banking led him to believe regulation "should be goal-oriented, not process-oriented...should not discourage appropriate changes in technology and market structure..., taking advantage of market mechanisms and using incentive-compatible approaches."
